alex: Quick heads-up — ran a set of microbenchmarks across Llama-3b, Mixtral-7B, and Qwen-7B with AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 profiles. Seeing a consistent p95 latency bump when the batcher switches kernels on RoPE-heavy prompts. Logs + numbers below, looking for ideas on kernel selection and KV cache heuristics.

maria: can you paste the exact command + seed? also which calibration prompts for AWQ?

alex: command: `./perf_runner --model {model} --quant {awq,gptq,fp8} --batcher heuristic --seq 1024 --kv-policy adaptive --calib prompts/calib_small.txt`
seed: 42
calib snippet: `prompts/calib_small.txt` contains 150 short Q/A pairs and 20 long-context tokens for RoPE scaling test.

perf-bot: Alert: perf-regression detected on 2025-11-12 10:12 UTC — job 1768504321 — p95 increased by 18% for Mixtral-7B AWQ (baseline: 84ms -> current: 99ms). See /logs/1768504321.

tess: quick profile dump from the Mixtral AWQ run (trimmed):
```
Model: mixtral-7b-awq
batch_size: dynamic (prefers 4)
seq_len: 1024
mean_latency_ms: 58
p95_latency_ms: 99
tokens_per_sec: 420
kv_lookup_pct: 23%
kernel_switches_per_req: 2.1
most_used_kernel: matmul_fp32_fast (fallback to int8_accel on seq>768)
```

ryan: that 'kernel_switches_per_req' is a red flag. looks like the batcher heuristics are picking fp32 matmuls early then evicting to int8 kernels mid-request when kv-cache misses increases latency. probably due to adaptive kv-policy thresholds being too aggressive.

maria: i compared AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 on the small eval (same 200 prompts):
- mixtral AWQ: acc_delta vs fp32: -0.9% (calib prompts used)
- mixtral GPTQ: acc_delta: -0.4%
- mixtral FP8: acc_delta: -0.3% but higher instability on long contexts
latency (p95): AWQ 99ms, GPTQ 92ms, FP8 86ms (on same hw)

alex: interesting — AWQ is worse latency and accuracy delta small but regression noted. maybe AWQ kernel isn't well-optimized for RoPE-scaling contexts.

tess: i pulled kernel traces — when seq > 768, we see this pattern: first tokens use `matmul_fp32_fast` (low-latency), then after kv-cache growth we call `kv_merge` and fall back to `int8_accel_conv` which has higher latency due to memory copies. config snippet:
```
batcher:
  policy: heuristic
  heuristics:
    prefer_throughput_threshold: 350 # tps
    kernel_stability_window: 3
kv:
  policy: adaptive
  eviction_threshold: 0.6
  merge_on_miss: true
kernel_selector:
  prefer_fp8_if_throughput_gt: 400
```

ryan: propose two quick experiments:
1) bump `kernel_stability_window` to 10 so we avoid switching mid-request.
2) increase `eviction_threshold` to 0.8 to keep KV entries longer (should reduce `kv_lookup_pct` spikes).

maria: +1. i'll run experiment matrix (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) x (window 3/10) x (evict 0.6/0.8) on a 2h job. also will test RoPE scaling factor tunings: default, 1.02, 0.98. include eval for generation PPL and exact-match on the eval set.

perf-bot: Job queued: perf_jobs/1768504321-experiments — estimated runtime 2h 10m.

alex: also add a targeted test where we force kernel_selector to prefer `int8_accel_conv` from start for AWQ to see if avoiding the switch helps end-to-end latency (even if single-token kernel slower, avoidance of copy might improve p95).

tess: note: for Mixtral FP8 kernel we still have a memcpy path when kv cache > 1.2GB. so for long contexts consider enabling streaming-kv (partial) to keep mem below threshold.

ryan: regarding RoPE scaling — earlier notes: scaling >1.0 reduces some hallucination on long prompts but increases token-by-token compute (more attention ops), so expect latency tradeoffs. keep as separate axis.

maria: initial quick results (first 30 mins):
- AWQ, window=3, evict=0.6: p95 99ms, tokens/sec 420, acc_delta -0.9%
- AWQ, window=10, evict=0.6: p95 91ms, tokens/sec 450, acc_delta -0.9%
- AWQ, window=10, evict=0.8: p95 86ms, tokens/sec 480, acc_delta -0.9%
- GPTQ, window=10, evict=0.8: p95 84ms, tokens/sec 495, acc_delta -0.4%
- FP8, window=10, evict=0.8: p95 80ms, tokens/sec 520, acc_delta -0.3%

alex: wow — increasing window/eviction helped AWQ a lot. suggests kernel switching and kv churn were main causes.

tess: next steps: make `kernel_stability_window` configurable per-model and tune default for Mixtral at 8-12. consider a quick heuristic: if seq_len median > 512 then window = 10.

ryan: i'll open a PR with kernel selector change: prefer stable kernels for first N tokens, and expose `stability_window` as runtime flag. link when ready.

maria: i'll finish full 2h runs and dump the full matrices + calib prompt accuracy reports to the shared run.

alex: plan sounds good. owners: ryan (kernel selector PR), tess (kv/streaming followups), maria (full perf matrix + accuracy), alex (priority triage + release notes).

alex: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow if matrices show regressions or odd tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
